What I perceived from trailer was it's a story about a teen who is rowdy and makes mistake the kind one makes in their teens. She further is brought to right values due to intervention from grandparents. Something like shown in movie Baghban.

The real story is the teen loses her grandmother because of her actions. She is not bad but things go wrong. She tries to cheer up her grandfather and is getting everything in place when her grandpa discovers the truth. He is now hurt. Will she succeed?

The teen girl gets an opportunity to write a play for her academics. She pens down her story. By the end of story we come to know the movie is inspired from true events. The other thing we crave is grandfather's forgiveness. Will that happen?

When I first saw the trailer, I thought it would be on the terms of teen being wasted but it's not the case. She is just fine given her age.

The most cherished character is played by Grandfather Pankaj Kapur. Others too have done justice to their roles.

Final Verdict: It's an above average drama that is sure to make u feel good at least for once.

Just watch it guys.

A truly fantastic film. I sincerely wish it had released on the big screen and received even greater success than Saiyaara or Dhurandhar. This is a must-watch movie for all three generations-grandchildren, children, parents, and grandparents alike.

It's hard to say who performed better than whom; every actor delivered a remarkable performance. But one thing is certain-whenever Pankaj Sir is part of a project, quality is guaranteed.

Everyone was outstanding, perfectly aligned with the film's beautiful message.

"Binny and Family" is a heartwarming Hindi film that captures the complexities of immigrant life, particularly the dynamics between generations. As a first-generation immigrant in Canada, I found this film deeply relatable, especially in how it explores the cultural gap and love between the older and younger generations in immigrant families.

The story revolves around Binny, a young teenage girl, navigating her life in UK, while her traditional Indian grandparents struggle to adjust to the cultural differences when they visit her every year in summers. The movie beautifully illustrates the gap between the expectations of the older generation and the aspirations of the younger, highlighting the misunderstandings that often arise. Binny, eager to fit into her new environment in each summers, embraces modern values, while her grandparents hold tightly to their cultural roots, leading to moments of frustration, confusion, and conflict.

What I found most resonant was how the film portrays the importance of intergenerational understanding. As someone who has seen this dynamic unfold in my own family, I appreciated how Binny and Family emphasizes that the older generation-represented by the grandparents-must make an active effort to understand and support the younger generation's desire for independence and change. It's not about abandoning tradition, but about finding common ground that allows both sides to grow together.

One of the standout moments in the film is when Binny's grandfather finally open up to new experiences and perspectives, realizing that by embracing the world their granddaughter is growing up in, they can foster a deeper connection. This turning point was especially poignant, as it reminded me of the journey many immigrant families go through, where the key to harmony lies in mutual respect and adaptability.

The message of Binny and Family is clear: while the younger generation must honor their heritage, it is equally crucial for the older generation to make a pleasant and fruitful effort to understand and accept the new world their grandchildren live in. This theme deeply resonated with me, as I've witnessed the transformative power of such understanding within my own immigrant family.

In summary, Binny and Family is a touching, relatable film that speaks to the immigrant experience across generations. It beautifully underscores the importance of empathy, communication, and compromise in maintaining strong family ties in a foreign land.

Let's support good cinema and watch this movie.
